name: Seweryn Goszczyński
credit: Anonymous photograph, before 1876 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Seweryn Goszczyński (1801–1876) was a Polish Romantic poet born in Ukraine, one of the writers of the so-called Ukrainian school together with Antoni Malczewski and Bohdan Zaleski. He took part in the November Uprising of 1830–31 and afterwards lived in exile.

His best-known work is the narrative poem Zamek kaniowski (Warsaw, 1828), set during the 1768 haidamak rising in Ukraine, which is the work included here. He also wrote prose, notably an account of a journey in the Tatra mountains, and died in 1876.
